# Remove the task checkbox UI from the plan viewer editor

## Pre-Implementation

Invoke `Skill(autopilot:branch-create)` with the resolved issue number `246`. The branch-create skill fetches the issue, generates an `issue-246-<slug>` branch name, and prompts the user to confirm before creation. Do NOT present a Hotfix/Trivial/Maintenance prefix prompt — issue inputs always use the `issue-<number>-<slug>` convention so the PR can link back via `Closes #246`.

The branch MUST be cut from `origin/main`, not from the current `opal-wren` worktree branch: `opal-wren` carries 6 unmerged commits from the unrelated overlay-cancel flake investigation (#236), and stacking on them would mix two changes into one PR.

## Summary

Remove the GFM task-checkbox widget from the plan viewer so `- [ ]` / `- [x]` items render as ordinary bullets, with a done item shown struck through instead of checked. Delete the editor-side toggle write path that only the checkbox could reach; keep the `@symbiot/annotations` task machinery, because drafts already saved on the current build can carry task toggles that must still load and be removable.

Steelmanned intent: Strip the unintended, visually poor task-checkbox affordance out of the plan reading surface without losing the done/open distinction, breaking task-list rendering, or orphaning task toggles sitting in users' saved drafts.

Score: 97/100

## Context

The checkbox arrived as three commits carried inside an unrelated palette PR, [#210](https://github.com/awinogradov/symbiot/pull/210) *"MAINTENANCE: Adopt a GitHub-style palette across the plan viewer"* — none of them announced by its title or body:

- [9002121](https://github.com/awinogradov/symbiot/commit/9002121) `fix(editor): render checkboxes for task list items`
- [62ec60c](https://github.com/awinogradov/symbiot/commit/62ec60c) `feat(editor): record task checkbox toggles as feedback` (22 files: a `T` tuple in the share codec, `task_<id>` marks, sidebar projection, feedback markdown)
- [a9d5be8](https://github.com/awinogradov/symbiot/commit/a9d5be8) `test(e2e): add task checkbox toggle scenario`

Three findings shape the removal.

**A plain `git revert` of the render commit is unsafe.** `todo` is not a valid CSS `list-style-type`. `ListElement` decides ordered-vs-unordered with `!ULIST_STYLE_TYPES.includes(listStyleType)`, and `"todo"` is not in that set — so with the `todo` branch simply deleted, task items fall through to `<ol>` and render as **decimal-numbered items**. That is the exact bug 9002121 was fixing. The `todo` case has to survive as a *bullet* case, minus the widget.

**Dropping the checkbox drops the only signal of done-ness.** The markdown deserializer eats the literal `[ ]` / `[x]` text and turns it into a `checked` boolean on the element, so with the checkbox gone a completed task and an open task would render as byte-identical bullets. Nothing serializes the Plate value back to markdown (the viewer is annotate-only; feedback is generated from annotations), so this is a *rendering* loss, not data loss — but it is a real one. A checked item therefore renders **struck through** instead.

**Task toggles may already exist in persisted drafts.** `useReviewState` persists the raw Plate value via `saveDraft(snapshotToDraft(snapshot))`, and that value carries `checked` + `taskOriginal` + `task_<id>` marks. Anyone who has clicked a checkbox on the current build has a saved draft containing a task toggle. Those drafts still load, `walkAnnotations` still finds the marks, and the sidebar still shows a removable task entry — so the **read and remove** paths must keep working even though the **create** path disappears.

That last split is what makes the cut clean:

```text
    CREATE (delete — only the checkbox could reach it)          READ / REMOVE (keep — saved drafts still hit it)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  checkbox <input> in ListElement.TodoList    │            │  walkAnnotations  → task_<id> marks → entries     │
  │        │ onChange                            │            │  sidebarProjection → "Mark as done" row           │
  │        ▼                                     │            │  serializeFeedback → agent markdown               │
  │  TaskToggleContext ─▶ useTaskToggle          │            │  T tuple in encode / decode                       │
  │        │                                     │            │  useRemoveAnnotation(kind: "task")                │
  │        ▼                                     │            │        │                                         │
  │  applyTaskToggle(editor, element)            │            │        ▼                                         │
  │        └─▶ writes checked + task_<id> marks  │            │  removeTaskToggle(editor, id)  ◀── still needed   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘            └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Rewrite the ListElement tests (failing-first)

`packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ListElement.test.tsx` — replace the two checkbox tests ("renders a read-only checkbox for todo items reflecting checked state", "renders an unchecked checkbox for open todo items") with two tests pinning the new contract:

- **open task** (`listStyleType: "todo"`): renders `UL`, `data-list-type="todo"`, inline `list-style-type: disc`, `data-checked="false"`, **no** `[data-testid="editor-task-checkbox"]` node, no strike class, and its text content.
- **done task** (`listStyleType: "todo", checked: true`): same, but `data-checked="true"` and the `<li>` carries the strike class.

Keep the existing `disc` and `decimal` tests untouched. The decimal one is the load-bearing regression guard: it is what proves `"todo"` did not leak back into the ordered branch.

verify: `bun run test --filter @symbiot/editor` — the two new tests fail (checkbox still rendered), the disc/decimal tests still pass.

### 2. Render task items as struck-through bullets

`packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ListElement.tsx` — delete the `TodoList` component entirely (the `<input type="checkbox">`, its `contentEditable={false}` gutter span, the `-ml-6` marker pull, the `accent-task-done` classes) along with the `todo` early-return, the `TaskToggleContext` import, and the now-unused `use` / `useCallback` imports.

Fold `"todo"` into the single generic path. **Resolve the alias once**, not in two places — an exclusion inside `isOrderedStyle` *and* a mapping inside `markerStyle` can drift apart, and each half-fix fails silently and differently (fix only the predicate → `<ul>` with an invalid `list-style-type: todo`, i.e. **no marker at all**; fix only the style → `<ol>` with a disc marker). One resolver makes that impossible:

```ts
/**
 * `todo` is a Plate list style, not a CSS one — left unmapped it renders no
 * marker, and left out of this alias it fails the unordered membership test
 * and falls through to decimal `<ol>` numbering. Resolve it to `disc` once,
 * before both the ordered check and the marker style read it.
 */
const listStyleAliases: Record<string, string> = { todo: "disc" };
```

Derive everything downstream from the resolved value, so a task item is simply an unordered `disc` list. Two things stay keyed off the *original* `"todo"`, because they carry the source semantics the alias erases:

- `data-list-type="todo"` — the BDD/unit selector surface (`docs/08-testing.md` mandates `data-testid`/data-attribute selectors; collapsing this to `"unordered"` would throw away the distinction for no gain).
- `data-checked={checked}` — keeps done-ness queryable from tests and CSS now that no `<input>` carries it.

Render the done state with `cn()` (from `@symbiot/ui`, already the project's conditional-class helper) on the `<li>`: `line-through` plus `text-muted-foreground`. Keep the `<li>` rendering `{children}` **directly** — no wrapper span. The old `<span className="min-w-0">` and the `contentEditable={false}` island go away with `TodoList`, and that is a bonus, not a risk: that span was an unmanaged non-editable DOM node inside the editable subtree, precisely the shape that corrupts Slate's DOM→model point mapping when a decoration range lands on it.

Contrast gate: `--muted-foreground` is currently gated only against `--muted`, not `--background`. Struck task text sits on `--background`, so add that pair to `packages/tailwind-config/contrast.test.ts`. If it does not clear AA, drop the color and ship `line-through` alone — strikethrough is a text decoration, not color, so it satisfies WCAG 1.4.1 (use of color) on its own.

verify: `bun run test --filter @symbiot/editor` — step 1's tests now green; `bun run test --filter tailwind-config` — the new contrast pair passes AA.

### 3. Delete the toggle write path

Three orphans that only the checkbox could reach:

- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/TaskToggleContext.ts` — delete the file (its sole consumer was `TodoList`).
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditor.tsx` — drop the `useTaskToggle` import + call and unwrap the `<TaskToggleContext value={onToggleTask}>` provider from around `<Plate>`.
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditorAuthoring.tsx` — delete the `useTaskToggle` hook and its `applyTaskToggle` import.

verify: `bun run typecheck && bun run lint` — no unresolved imports, no unused exports. Plus the grep gate in the Verification section (typecheck and lint alone will not catch a stale `onToggleTask` prop threaded from a caller, or a leftover `editor-task-checkbox` selector in a doc or step file).

### 4. Cut `applyTaskToggle.ts` down to the remove path

Rename `packages/symbiot-editor/src/utils/applyTaskToggle.ts` → `removeTaskToggle.ts`; the file would otherwise be named for an export it no longer has.

- Delete `applyTaskToggle` and the two helpers only it used: `findElementPath` and `setLeafMarks`.
- Keep `removeTaskToggle` and its live dependencies: `isTextLeaf`, `isElement`, `collectTextLeafPaths`, `taskIdOfLeaf`, `findTaskId`, `findTaskItem`, `unsetLeafMarks`.
- Repoint the import in `ReviewEditorAuthoring.tsx`. `useRemoveAnnotation`'s `kind === "task"` branch stays, as does `RemovableAnnotationKind = AnnotationHandleKind | "task"` in `ReviewEditorTypes.tsx` — a saved draft can still surface a removable task entry.

Rename `applyTaskToggle.test.ts` → `removeTaskToggle.test.ts` and drop the `applyTaskToggle` describe block. The surviving `removeTaskToggle` cases currently *build* their fixture by calling `applyTaskToggle` first, so they must now construct the marked Plate value directly: an element with `checked` + `taskOriginal`, and a text leaf carrying `task: true` + `task_<id>: true`.

That hand-built fixture is not a test convenience — once `applyTaskToggle` is deleted it becomes the **only** remaining specification of a shape that real saved drafts are frozen in. Comment it as such (frozen legacy draft shape, produced by `applyTaskToggle` before its removal in this change), so a later "cleanup" of `taskOriginal` or the bare `task: true` mark cannot silently turn `removeTaskToggle` into a no-op against real user data while the test stays green.

verify: `bun run test --filter @symbiot/editor` — `removeTaskToggle.test.ts` green on both the "removes marks and restores `taskOriginal`" and the "no-ops on a missing id" cases.

### 5. Delete the e2e scenario

The BDD scenario clicks the checkbox, so it cannot survive:

- `features/uc3-annotate-doc/task-checkbox.feature` — delete.
- `features/steps/task.steps.ts` — delete; both its steps (`I toggle task checkbox {int}`, `the annotation sidebar shows a task entry {string}`) are used only by that feature.

**Known coverage exposure — measure, do not assume.** This scenario was the only thing exercising the task branches in `apps/viewer/src/client/utils/sidebarProjection.ts` (`taskBody`, the `kind === "task"` projection) and `useReviewState.ts`. `apps/**` is excluded from the *unit* gate (`vitest.config.ts`, 90% lines/statements/branches) and measured only by the **BDD** coverage report — so deleting this feature leaves those branches uncovered there and can push the BDD gate red. `sidebarProjection.ts` has no unit test today.

If the BDD gate does go red on exactly those branches, that is a real signal rather than the known flake (the per-port theme-bootstrap flake was fixed in #168): it means the retained-but-dormant task machinery has no test at all. The fix in that case is a unit test for `sidebarProjection`'s task projection — not deleting the machinery, which the saved-draft path still needs.

verify: `bun run test:e2e` — suite green, no undefined step definitions. Then `bun run test:e2e:coverage` and compare the BDD summary against the pre-change run; branches must hold ≥ 90%.

### 6. Harden the tuple decoder against unknown kinds

`packages/symbiot-annotations/src/decode.ts` — `decodeAnnotations` looks up `decoders[tuple[0]]` and calls the result unconditionally, so a tuple kind this build does not know throws a `TypeError` and takes the entire share link down with it. Make it skip unrecognized kinds and decode the rest.

**Map first, then filter.** Each decoder receives the tuple's array index `i` and synthesizes the entry id from it (`c-${index}`, `t-${index}`, …). Filtering the tuples *before* mapping would renumber every entry after a skipped one and silently shift those ids. Map over the original array (yielding `undefined` for unknown kinds), then drop the `undefined`s — original indices preserved.

verify: new cases in `packages/symbiot-annotations/src/decode.test.ts` — a list with an **unknown kind first**, followed by a valid `C`, decodes to just the comment entry *and* that entry keeps its original index-derived id (`c-1`, not `c-0`). Placing the unknown tuple last would pass even with the buggy filter-first implementation, so the ordering in this test is the whole point.

Current share-codec goldens (`fixtures/golden/share-codec/*.json`) contain no `T` tuple, so nothing is broken today — this is the robustness that makes the *next* kind removal safe, and it is what you asked for when choosing "ignore unknown tuples" over a hard removal.

## Files

- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ListElement.test.tsx` — swap the two checkbox tests for open/done bullet tests (written first)
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ListElement.tsx` — delete `TodoList`; resolve `"todo"` → `disc` once; strike + `data-checked` on done items
- `packages/tailwind-config/contrast.test.ts` — gate `--muted-foreground` on `--background`
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/TaskToggleContext.ts` — delete
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditor.tsx` — drop the provider + `useTaskToggle`
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditorAuthoring.tsx` — delete `useTaskToggle`; repoint the `removeTaskToggle` import
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/utils/applyTaskToggle.ts` — rename to `removeTaskToggle.ts`; drop `applyTaskToggle`, `findElementPath`, `setLeafMarks`
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/utils/applyTaskToggle.test.ts` — rename to `removeTaskToggle.test.ts`; build the frozen legacy-draft fixture directly
- `features/uc3-annotate-doc/task-checkbox.feature` — delete
- `features/steps/task.steps.ts` — delete
- `packages/symbiot-annotations/src/decode.ts` — map-then-filter unknown tuple kinds
- `packages/symbiot-annotations/src/decode.test.ts` — unknown-kind-first case, asserting ids do not shift
- `docs/05-theming.md` — retarget the two `--task-done` mentions (see Post-Implementation)

## Not changing

Deliberately out of scope, so a reviewer does not read these as omissions:

- `packages/symbiot-annotations` task machinery — the `T` tuple, `walkAnnotations`' `task_<id>` reader, `onlyTasks`, `serializeFeedback`'s task formatting, `fixtures/golden/task.md`. Still reachable from saved drafts, and still covered by their own unit tests (the golden test synthesizes its entries directly rather than driving the UI, so it stays green).
- `apps/viewer/src/client/utils/sidebarProjection.ts` and `useReviewState.ts` task branches — the sidebar must still render and remove a task entry from an existing draft.
- `packages/symbiot-ui/src/components/AnnotationSidebarTypes.tsx` — the `task` label / color / confirm-copy rows, for the same reason.
- The `--task-done` token — still consumed as `text-task-done` by the sidebar's task row. Only the `accent-task-done` *usage* disappears; the token and its `@theme inline` registration stay.
- Screen-reader announcement of done-ness. The checkbox carried `aria-label="Completed task" / "Open task"`; strikethrough does not replace it. Restoring it would mean injecting a visually-hidden `contentEditable={false}` span back into the editable subtree — the same DOM island step 2 is removing. Accepted trade-off; the checkbox was never listed in the ARIA-label inventory in `docs/06-a11y.md`, so no inventory row is being retired.

## Verification

Full gate, in order:

1. `bun run typecheck` — catches any missed import of the deleted `TaskToggleContext` / `applyTaskToggle`.
2. `bun run lint` — catches unused exports and orphaned imports (CLAUDE.md §14: no unused exports).
3. **Grep sweep** — `rg -n 'editor-task-checkbox|TaskToggleContext|applyTaskToggle|useTaskToggle|onToggleTask|TodoList|accent-task-done'` must return **zero** hits outside the git history. `typecheck` and `lint` will not flag a stale `data-testid` in a feature file, a doc, or a leftover Tailwind class.
4. `bun run test` — unit suites for `@symbiot/editor` (list rendering incl. the decimal regression guard, `removeTaskToggle`), `@symbiot/annotations` (golden `task.md` byte-equality still passes, new unknown-kind decode cases), `@symbiot/ui`, `tailwind-config` (new contrast pair). content.text:
Plan validated at 97/100. Here's what the investigation turned up and how the plan responds.

**Where it came from:** the checkbox wasn't a deliberate feature — it rode into `main` inside PR [#210](https://github.com/awinogradov/symbiot/pull/210), a *GitHub-palette* PR, as three commits its title and body never mention. One of them ([62ec60c](https://github.com/awinogradov/symbiot/commit/62ec60c), 22 files) is a whole feedback channel: clicking a checkbox becomes a `T` annotation in the share codec and lands in the agent's feedback markdown.

**Three things a naive revert would have broken**, all now handled:

1. Reverting the render commit alone makes `- [ ]` items render as a **numbered list** — `todo` isn't a valid CSS `list-style-type`, so it falls through to `<ol>`. That's the bug the commit was fixing. The plan keeps a `todo` case that resolves to a disc bullet, via a single alias so the two halves can't drift apart.
2. Removing the checkbox removes the **only signal of done-ness** — the `[x]` text is eaten by the parser, so done and open tasks would look identical. You chose strikethrough, so done items render struck through with a `data-checked` hook.
3. Drafts are persisted as the raw Plate value, so anyone who already clicked a checkbox has **`task_<id>` marks saved on disk**. That's why `removeTaskToggle` and the annotations machinery stay — they're the read path for existing drafts, not dead code. Only the create path (`applyTaskToggle`, `TaskToggleContext`, `useTaskToggle`) is deleted.

# Remove the task checkbox UI from the plan viewer editor

## Pre-Implementation

Invoke `Skill(autopilot:branch-create)` with the resolved issue number `246`. The branch-create skill fetches the issue, generates an `issue-246-<slug>` branch name, and prompts the user to confirm before creation. Do NOT present a Hotfix/Trivial/Maintenance prefix prompt — issue inputs always use the `issue-<number>-<slug>` convention so the PR can link back via `Closes #246`.

The branch MUST be cut from `origin/main`, not from the current `opal-wren` worktree branch: `opal-wren` carries 6 unmerged commits from the unrelated overlay-cancel flake investigation (#236), and stacking on them would mix two changes into one PR.

## Summary

Remove the GFM task-checkbox widget from the plan viewer so `- [ ]` / `- [x]` items render as ordinary bullets, with a done item shown struck through instead of checked. Delete the editor-side toggle write path that only the checkbox could reach; keep the `@symbiot/annotations` task machinery, because drafts already saved on the current build can carry task toggles that must still load and be removable.

Steelmanned intent: Strip the unintended, visually poor task-checkbox affordance out of the plan reading surface without losing the done/open distinction, breaking task-list rendering, or orphaning task toggles sitting in users' saved drafts.

Score: 97/100

## Context

The checkbox arrived as three commits carried inside an unrelated palette PR, [#210](https://github.com/awinogradov/symbiot/pull/210) *"MAINTENANCE: Adopt a GitHub-style palette across the plan viewer"* — none of them announced by its title or body:

- [9002121](https://github.com/awinogradov/symbiot/commit/9002121) `fix(editor): render checkboxes for task list items`
- [62ec60c](https://github.com/awinogradov/symbiot/commit/62ec60c) `feat(editor): record task checkbox toggles as feedback` (22 files: a `T` tuple in the share codec, `task_<id>` marks, sidebar projection, feedback markdown)
- [a9d5be8](https://github.com/awinogradov/symbiot/commit/a9d5be8) `test(e2e): add task checkbox toggle scenario`

Three findings shape the removal.

**A plain `git revert` of the render commit is unsafe.** `todo` is not a valid CSS `list-style-type`. `ListElement` decides ordered-vs-unordered with `!ULIST_STYLE_TYPES.includes(listStyleType)`, and `"todo"` is not in that set — so with the `todo` branch simply deleted, task items fall through to `<ol>` and render as **decimal-numbered items**. That is the exact bug 9002121 was fixing. The `todo` case has to survive as a *bullet* case, minus the widget.

**Dropping the checkbox drops the only signal of done-ness.** The markdown deserializer eats the literal `[ ]` / `[x]` text and turns it into a `checked` boolean on the element, so with the checkbox gone a completed task and an open task would render as byte-identical bullets. Nothing serializes the Plate value back to markdown (the viewer is annotate-only; feedback is generated from annotations), so this is a *rendering* loss, not data loss — but it is a real one. A checked item therefore renders **struck through** instead.

**Task toggles may already exist in persisted drafts.** `useReviewState` persists the raw Plate value via `saveDraft(snapshotToDraft(snapshot))`, and that value carries `checked` + `taskOriginal` + `task_<id>` marks. Anyone who has clicked a checkbox on the current build has a saved draft containing a task toggle. Those drafts still load, `walkAnnotations` still finds the marks, and the sidebar still shows a removable task entry — so the **read and remove** paths must keep working even though the **create** path disappears.

That last split is what makes the cut clean:

```text
    CREATE (delete — only the checkbox could reach it)          READ / REMOVE (keep — saved drafts still hit it)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  checkbox <input> in ListElement.TodoList    │            │  walkAnnotations  → task_<id> marks → entries     │
  │        │ onChange                            │            │  sidebarProjection → "Mark as done" row           │
  │        ▼                                     │            │  serializeFeedback → agent markdown               │
  │  TaskToggleContext ─▶ useTaskToggle          │            │  T tuple in encode / decode                       │
  │        │                                     │            │  useRemoveAnnotation(kind: "task")                │
  │        ▼                                     │            │        │                                         │
  │  applyTaskToggle(editor, element)            │            │        ▼                                         │
  │        └─▶ writes checked + task_<id> marks  │            │  removeTaskToggle(editor, id)  ◀── still needed   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘            └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 1. Rewrite the ListElement tests (failing-first)

`packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ListElement.test.tsx` — replace the two checkbox tests ("renders a read-only checkbox for todo items reflecting checked state", "renders an unchecked checkbox for open todo items") with two tests pinning the new contract:

- **open task** (`listStyleType: "todo"`): renders `UL`, `data-list-type="todo"`, inline `list-style-type: disc`, `data-checked="false"`, **no** `[data-testid="editor-task-checkbox"]` node, no strike class, and its text content.
- **done task** (`listStyleType: "todo", checked: true`): same, but `data-checked="true"` and the `<li>` carries the strike class.

Keep the existing `disc` and `decimal` tests untouched. The decimal one is the load-bearing regression guard: it is what proves `"todo"` did not leak back into the ordered branch.

verify: `bun run test --filter @symbiot/editor` — the two new tests fail (checkbox still rendered), the disc/decimal tests still pass.

### 2. Render task items as struck-through bullets

`packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ListElement.tsx` — delete the `TodoList` component entirely (the `<input type="checkbox">`, its `contentEditable={false}` gutter span, the `-ml-6` marker pull, the `accent-task-done` classes) along with the `todo` early-return, the `TaskToggleContext` import, and the now-unused `use` / `useCallback` imports.

Fold `"todo"` into the single generic path. **Resolve the alias once**, not in two places — an exclusion inside `isOrderedStyle` *and* a mapping inside `markerStyle` can drift apart, and each half-fix fails silently and differently (fix only the predicate → `<ul>` with an invalid `list-style-type: todo`, i.e. **no marker at all**; fix only the style → `<ol>` with a disc marker). One resolver makes that impossible:

```ts
/**
 * `todo` is a Plate list style, not a CSS one — left unmapped it renders no
 * marker, and left out of this alias it fails the unordered membership test
 * and falls through to decimal `<ol>` numbering. Resolve it to `disc` once,
 * before both the ordered check and the marker style read it.
 */
const listStyleAliases: Record<string, string> = { todo: "disc" };
```

Derive everything downstream from the resolved value, so a task item is simply an unordered `disc` list. Two things stay keyed off the *original* `"todo"`, because they carry the source semantics the alias erases:

- `data-list-type="todo"` — the BDD/unit selector surface (`docs/08-testing.md` mandates `data-testid`/data-attribute selectors; collapsing this to `"unordered"` would throw away the distinction for no gain).
- `data-checked={checked}` — keeps done-ness queryable from tests and CSS now that no `<input>` carries it.

Render the done state with `cn()` (from `@symbiot/ui`, already the project's conditional-class helper) on the `<li>`: `line-through` plus `text-muted-foreground`. Keep the `<li>` rendering `{children}` **directly** — no wrapper span. The old `<span className="min-w-0">` and the `contentEditable={false}` island go away with `TodoList`, and that is a bonus, not a risk: that span was an unmanaged non-editable DOM node inside the editable subtree, precisely the shape that corrupts Slate's DOM→model point mapping when a decoration range lands on it.

Contrast gate: `--muted-foreground` is currently gated only against `--muted`, not `--background`. Struck task text sits on `--background`, so add that pair to `packages/tailwind-config/contrast.test.ts`. If it does not clear AA, drop the color and ship `line-through` alone — strikethrough is a text decoration, not color, so it satisfies WCAG 1.4.1 (use of color) on its own.

verify: `bun run test --filter @symbiot/editor` — step 1's tests now green; `bun run test --filter tailwind-config` — the new contrast pair passes AA.

### 3. Delete the toggle write path

Three orphans that only the checkbox could reach:

- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/TaskToggleContext.ts` — delete the file (its sole consumer was `TodoList`).
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditor.tsx` — drop the `useTaskToggle` import + call and unwrap the `<TaskToggleContext value={onToggleTask}>` provider from around `<Plate>`.
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditorAuthoring.tsx` — delete the `useTaskToggle` hook and its `applyTaskToggle` import.

verify: `bun run typecheck && bun run lint` — no unresolved imports, no unused exports. Plus the grep gate in the Verification section (typecheck and lint alone will not catch a stale `onToggleTask` prop threaded from a caller, or a leftover `editor-task-checkbox` selector in a doc or step file).

### 4. Cut `applyTaskToggle.ts` down to the remove path

Rename `packages/symbiot-editor/src/utils/applyTaskToggle.ts` → `removeTaskToggle.ts`; the file would otherwise be named for an export it no longer has.

- Delete `applyTaskToggle` and the two helpers only it used: `findElementPath` and `setLeafMarks`.
- Keep `removeTaskToggle` and its live dependencies: `isTextLeaf`, `isElement`, `collectTextLeafPaths`, `taskIdOfLeaf`, `findTaskId`, `findTaskItem`, `unsetLeafMarks`.
- Repoint the import in `ReviewEditorAuthoring.tsx`. `useRemoveAnnotation`'s `kind === "task"` branch stays, as does `RemovableAnnotationKind = AnnotationHandleKind | "task"` in `ReviewEditorTypes.tsx` — a saved draft can still surface a removable task entry.

Rename `applyTaskToggle.test.ts` → `removeTaskToggle.test.ts` and drop the `applyTaskToggle` describe block. The surviving `removeTaskToggle` cases currently *build* their fixture by calling `applyTaskToggle` first, so they must now construct the marked Plate value directly: an element with `checked` + `taskOriginal`, and a text leaf carrying `task: true` + `task_<id>: true`.

That hand-built fixture is not a test convenience — once `applyTaskToggle` is deleted it becomes the **only** remaining specification of a shape that real saved drafts are frozen in. Comment it as such (frozen legacy draft shape, produced by `applyTaskToggle` before its removal in this change), so a later "cleanup" of `taskOriginal` or the bare `task: true` mark cannot silently turn `removeTaskToggle` into a no-op against real user data while the test stays green.

verify: `bun run test --filter @symbiot/editor` — `removeTaskToggle.test.ts` green on both the "removes marks and restores `taskOriginal`" and the "no-ops on a missing id" cases.

### 5. Delete the e2e scenario

The BDD scenario clicks the checkbox, so it cannot survive:

- `features/uc3-annotate-doc/task-checkbox.feature` — delete.
- `features/steps/task.steps.ts` — delete; both its steps (`I toggle task checkbox {int}`, `the annotation sidebar shows a task entry {string}`) are used only by that feature.

**Known coverage exposure — measure, do not assume.** This scenario was the only thing exercising the task branches in `apps/viewer/src/client/utils/sidebarProjection.ts` (`taskBody`, the `kind === "task"` projection) and `useReviewState.ts`. `apps/**` is excluded from the *unit* gate (`vitest.config.ts`, 90% lines/statements/branches) and measured only by the **BDD** coverage report — so deleting this feature leaves those branches uncovered there and can push the BDD gate red. `sidebarProjection.ts` has no unit test today.

If the BDD gate does go red on exactly those branches, that is a real signal rather than the known flake (the per-port theme-bootstrap flake was fixed in #168): it means the retained-but-dormant task machinery has no test at all. The fix in that case is a unit test for `sidebarProjection`'s task projection — not deleting the machinery, which the saved-draft path still needs.

verify: `bun run test:e2e` — suite green, no undefined step definitions. Then `bun run test:e2e:coverage` and compare the BDD summary against the pre-change run; branches must hold ≥ 90%.

Filtering the tuples *before* mapping would renumber every entry after a skipped one and silently shift those ids. Map over the original array (yielding `undefined` for unknown kinds), then drop the `undefined`s — original indices preserved.

verify: new cases in `packages/symbiot-annotations/src/decode.test.ts` — a list with an **unknown kind first**, followed by a valid `C`, decodes to just the comment entry *and* that entry keeps its original index-derived id (`c-1`, not `c-0`). Placing the unknown tuple last would pass even with the buggy filter-first implementation, so the ordering in this test is the whole point.

Current share-codec goldens (`fixtures/golden/share-codec/*.json`) contain no `T` tuple, so nothing is broken today — this is the robustness that makes the *next* kind removal safe, and it is what you asked for when choosing "ignore unknown tuples" over a hard removal.

## Files

- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ListElement.test.tsx` — swap the two checkbox tests for open/done bullet tests (written first)
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ListElement.tsx` — delete `TodoList`; resolve `"todo"` → `disc` once; strike + `data-checked` on done items
- `packages/tailwind-config/contrast.test.ts` — gate `--muted-foreground` on `--background`
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/TaskToggleContext.ts` — delete
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditor.tsx` — drop the provider + `useTaskToggle`
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditorAuthoring.tsx` — delete `useTaskToggle`; repoint the `removeTaskToggle` import
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/utils/applyTaskToggle.ts` — rename to `removeTaskToggle.ts`; drop `applyTaskToggle`, `findElementPath`, `setLeafMarks`
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/utils/applyTaskToggle.test.ts` — rename to `removeTaskToggle.test.ts`; build the frozen legacy-draft fixture directly
- `features/uc3-annotate-doc/task-checkbox.feature` — delete
- `features/steps/task.steps.ts` — delete
- `packages/symbiot-annotations/src/decode.ts` — map-then-filter unknown tuple kinds
- `packages/symbiot-annotations/src/decode.test.ts` — unknown-kind-first case, asserting ids do not shift
- `docs/05-theming.md` — retarget the two `--task-done` mentions (see Post-Implementation)

## Not changing

Deliberately out of scope, so a reviewer does not read these as omissions:

- `packages/symbiot-annotations` task machinery — the `T` tuple, `walkAnnotations`' `task_<id>` reader, `onlyTasks`, `serializeFeedback`'s task formatting, `fixtures/golden/task.md`. Still reachable from saved drafts, and still covered by their own unit tests (the golden test synthesizes its entries directly rather than driving the UI, so it stays green).
- `apps/viewer/src/client/utils/sidebarProjection.ts` and `useReviewState.ts` task branches — the sidebar must still render and remove a task entry from an existing draft.
- `packages/symbiot-ui/src/components/AnnotationSidebarTypes.tsx` — the `task` label / color / confirm-copy rows, for the same reason.
- The `--task-done` token — still consumed as `text-task-done` by the sidebar's task row. Only the `accent-task-done` *usage* disappears; the token and its `@theme inline` registration stay.
- Screen-reader announcement of done-ness. The checkbox carried `aria-label="Completed task" / "Open task"`; strikethrough does not replace it. Restoring it would mean injecting a visually-hidden `contentEditable={false}` span back into the editable subtree — the same DOM island step 2 is removing. Accepted trade-off; the checkbox was never listed in the ARIA-label inventory in `docs/06-a11y.md`, so no inventory row is being retired.

## Verification

Full gate, in order:

1. `bun run typecheck` — catches any missed import of the deleted `TaskToggleContext` / `applyTaskToggle`.
2. `bun run lint` — catches unused exports and orphaned imports (CLAUDE.md §14: no unused exports).
3. **Grep sweep** — `rg -n 'editor-task-checkbox|TaskToggleContext|applyTaskToggle|useTaskToggle|onToggleTask|TodoList|accent-task-done'` must return **zero** hits outside the git history. `typecheck` and `lint` will not flag a stale `data-testid` in a feature file, a doc, or a leftover Tailwind class.
4. `bun run test` — unit suites for `@symbiot/editor` (list rendering incl. the decimal regression guard, `removeTaskToggle`), `@symbiot/annotations` (golden `task.md` byte-equality still passes, new unknown-kind decode cases), `@symbiot/ui`, `tailwind-config` (new contrast pair). Use `bun run test` (turbo), not a bare root `bun test` — the latter reports false jsdom failures in this repo.
5. `bun run test:e2e` — BDD suite with the task-checkbox feature removed; no undefined step definitions.
6. `bun run test:e2e:coverage` — BDD branch coverage still ≥ 90% after losing the task scenario (see step 5's coverage note).
7. **Manual check in the running viewer** — open a plan containing both `- [ ]` and `- [x]` items and confirm: bullets aligned with ordinary bullet lists, no checkbox, no decimal numbering, and the done item struck through.

## Post-Implementation

After all implementation steps and verification are complete:

1. **Update documentation (MANDATORY).** In `docs/05-theming.md`, two lines describe `--task-done` in terms of a checkbox that will no longer exist:
   - the token-table row `decorative checkbox accent — not gated` → describe it as the task-annotation accent (still ungated).
   - the sentence "`--task-done` is registered as the `accent-task-done` checkbox accent" → it is consumed as `text-task-done` by the sidebar's task row.

   If step 2 added the `--muted-foreground` / `--background` pair to the contrast test, add its ratios to that same table. No other doc claims the checkbox exists: `docs/03-server-contract.md` and `docs/08-testing.md` describe the feedback format and golden gate, both unchanged, and `docs/06-a11y.md` never listed the checkbox. The repository has no `rfc/` directory, so no RFC version bump applies.

2. Present next actions using AskUserQuestion.

This change is user-facing (the checkbox disappears from the plan surface), so use `--release-notes` in the "Create PR" option.

Tool parameters:
- `question`: "All changes implemented and verified. What's next?"
- `header`: "Next"
- `options`: [
  { label: "Create commit", description: "Run /autopilot:commits-create to commit changes" },
  { label: "Create PR", description: "Run /autopilot:pr-create --release-notes to open a PR with release notes" },
  { label: "Done", description: "No further action needed" }
  ]
- `multiSelect`: false

After the user selects their option:
- "Create commit": invoke `Skill(autopilot:commits-create)`
- "Create PR": invoke `Skill(autopilot:pr-create)` with the flags shown in the option description
- "Done": no further action needed

The old `<span className="min-w-0">` and the `contentEditable={false}` island go away with `TodoList`, and that is a bonus, not a risk: that span was an unmanaged non-editable DOM node inside the editable subtree, precisely the shape that corrupts Slate's DOM→model point mapping when a decoration range lands on it.

Contrast gate: `--muted-foreground` is currently gated only against `--muted`, not `--background`. Struck task text sits on `--background`, so add that pair to `packages/tailwind-config/contrast.test.ts`. If it does not clear AA, drop the color and ship `line-through` alone — strikethrough is a text decoration, not color, so it satisfies WCAG 1.4.1 (use of color) on its own.

verify: `bun run test --filter @symbiot/editor` — step 1's tests now green; `bun run test --filter tailwind-config` — the new contrast pair passes AA.

### 3. Delete the toggle write path

Three orphans that only the checkbox could reach:

- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/TaskToggleContext.ts` — delete the file (its sole consumer was `TodoList`).
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditor.tsx` — drop the `useTaskToggle` import + call and unwrap the `<TaskToggleContext value={onToggleTask}>` provider from around `<Plate>`.
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditorAuthoring.tsx` — delete the `useTaskToggle` hook and its `applyTaskToggle` import.

verify: `bun run typecheck && bun run lint` — no unresolved imports, no unused exports. Plus the grep gate in the Verification section (typecheck and lint alone will not catch a stale `onToggleTask` prop threaded from a caller, or a leftover `editor-task-checkbox` selector in a doc or step file).

### 4. Cut `applyTaskToggle.ts` down to the remove path

Rename `packages/symbiot-editor/src/utils/applyTaskToggle.ts` → `removeTaskToggle.ts`; the file would otherwise be named for an export it no longer has.

- Delete `applyTaskToggle` and the two helpers only it used: `findElementPath` and `setLeafMarks`.
- Keep `removeTaskToggle` and its live dependencies: `isTextLeaf`, `isElement`, `collectTextLeafPaths`, `taskIdOfLeaf`, `findTaskId`, `findTaskItem`, `unsetLeafMarks`.
- Repoint the import in `ReviewEditorAuthoring.tsx`. `useRemoveAnnotation`'s `kind === "task"` branch stays, as does `RemovableAnnotationKind = AnnotationHandleKind | "task"` in `ReviewEditorTypes.tsx` — a saved draft can still surface a removable task entry.

Rename `applyTaskToggle.test.ts` → `removeTaskToggle.test.ts` and drop the `applyTaskToggle` describe block. The surviving `removeTaskToggle` cases currently *build* their fixture by calling `applyTaskToggle` first, so they must now construct the marked Plate value directly: an element with `checked` + `taskOriginal`, and a text leaf carrying `task: true` + `task_<id>: true`.

That hand-built fixture is not a test convenience — once `applyTaskToggle` is deleted it becomes the **only** remaining specification of a shape that real saved drafts are frozen in. Comment it as such (frozen legacy draft shape, produced by `applyTaskToggle` before its removal in this change), so a later "cleanup" of `taskOriginal` or the bare `task: true` mark cannot silently turn `removeTaskToggle` into a no-op against real user data while the test stays green.

verify: `bun run test --filter @symbiot/editor` — `removeTaskToggle.test.ts` green on both the "removes marks and restores `taskOriginal`" and the "no-ops on a missing id" cases.

### 5. Delete the e2e scenario

The BDD scenario clicks the checkbox, so it cannot survive:

- `features/uc3-annotate-doc/task-checkbox.feature` — delete.
- `features/steps/task.steps.ts` — delete; both its steps (`I toggle task checkbox {int}`, `the annotation sidebar shows a task entry {string}`) are used only by that feature.

**Known coverage exposure — measure, do not assume.** This scenario was the only thing exercising the task branches in `apps/viewer/src/client/utils/sidebarProjection.ts` (`taskBody`, the `kind === "task"` projection) and `useReviewState.ts`. `apps/**` is excluded from the *unit* gate (`vitest.config.ts`, 90% lines/statements/branches) and measured only by the **BDD** coverage report — so deleting this feature leaves those branches uncovered there and can push the BDD gate red. `sidebarProjection.ts` has no unit test today.

If the BDD gate does go red on exactly those branches, that is a real signal rather than the known flake (the per-port theme-bootstrap flake was fixed in #168): it means the retained-but-dormant task machinery has no test at all. The fix in that case is a unit test for `sidebarProjection`'s task projection — not deleting the machinery, which the saved-draft path still needs.

verify: `bun run test:e2e` — suite green, no undefined step definitions. Then `bun run test:e2e:coverage` and compare the BDD summary against the pre-change run; branches must hold ≥ 90%.

### 6. Harden the tuple decoder against unknown kinds

`packages/symbiot-annotations/src/decode.ts` — `decodeAnnotations` looks up `decoders[tuple[0]]` and calls the result unconditionally, so a tuple kind this build does not know throws a `TypeError` and takes the entire share link down with it. Make it skip unrecognized kinds and decode the rest.

**Map first, then filter.** Each decoder receives the tuple's array index `i` and synthesizes the entry id from it (`c-${index}`, `t-${index}`, …). Filtering the tuples *before* mapping would renumber every entry after a skipped one and silently shift those ids. Map over the original array (yielding `undefined` for unknown kinds), then drop the `undefined`s — original indices preserved.

verify: new cases in `packages/symbiot-annotations/src/decode.test.ts` — a list with an **unknown kind first**, followed by a valid `C`, decodes to just the comment entry *and* that entry keeps its original index-derived id (`c-1`, not `c-0`). Placing the unknown tuple last would pass even with the buggy filter-first implementation, so the ordering in this test is the whole point.

Current share-codec goldens (`fixtures/golden/share-codec/*.json`) contain no `T` tuple, so nothing is broken today — this is the robustness that makes the *next* kind removal safe, and it is what you asked for when choosing "ignore unknown tuples" over a hard removal.

## Files

- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ListElement.test.tsx` — swap the two checkbox tests for open/done bullet tests (written first)
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ListElement.tsx` — delete `TodoList`; resolve `"todo"` → `disc` once; strike + `data-checked` on done items
- `packages/tailwind-config/contrast.test.ts` — gate `--muted-foreground` on `--background`
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/TaskToggleContext.ts` — delete
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditor.tsx` — drop the provider + `useTaskToggle`
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/components/ReviewEditorAuthoring.tsx` — delete `useTaskToggle`; repoint the `removeTaskToggle` import
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/utils/applyTaskToggle.ts` — rename to `removeTaskToggle.ts`; drop `applyTaskToggle`, `findElementPath`, `setLeafMarks`
- `packages/symbiot-editor/src/utils/applyTaskToggle.test.ts` — rename to `removeTaskToggle.test.ts`; build the frozen legacy-draft fixture directly
- `features/uc3-annotate-doc/task-checkbox.feature` — delete
- `features/steps/task.steps.ts` — delete
- `packages/symbiot-annotations/src/decode.ts` — map-then-filter unknown tuple kinds
- `packages/symbiot-annotations/src/decode.test.ts` — unknown-kind-first case, asserting ids do not shift
- `docs/05-theming.md` — retarget the two `--task-done` mentions (see Post-Implementation)

## Not changing

Deliberately out of scope, so a reviewer does not read these as omissions:

- `packages/symbiot-annotations` task machinery — the `T` tuple, `walkAnnotations`' `task_<id>` reader, `onlyTasks`, `serializeFeedback`'s task formatting, `fixtures/golden/task.md`. Still reachable from saved drafts, and still covered by their own unit tests (the golden test synthesizes its entries directly rather than driving the UI, so it stays green).
- `apps/viewer/src/client/utils/sidebarProjection.ts` and `useReviewState.ts` task branches — the sidebar must still render and remove a task entry from an existing draft.
- `packages/symbiot-ui/src/components/AnnotationSidebarTypes.tsx` — the `task` label / color / confirm-copy rows, for the same reason.
- The `--task-done` token — still consumed as `text-task-done` by the sidebar's task row. Only the `accent-task-done` *usage* disappears; the token and its `@theme inline` registration stay.
- Screen-reader announcement of done-ness. The checkbox carried `aria-label="Completed task" / "Open task"`; strikethrough does not replace it. Restoring it would mean injecting a visually-hidden `contentEditable={false}` span back into the editable subtree — the same DOM island step 2 is removing. Accepted trade-off; the checkbox was never listed in the ARIA-label inventory in `docs/06-a11y.md`, so no inventory row is being retired.

## Verification

Full gate, in order:

1. `bun run typecheck` — catches any missed import of the deleted `TaskToggleContext` / `applyTaskToggle`.
2. `bun run lint` — catches unused exports and orphaned imports (CLAUDE.md §14: no unused exports).
3. **Grep sweep** — `rg -n 'editor-task-checkbox|TaskToggleContext|applyTaskToggle|useTaskToggle|onToggleTask|TodoList|accent-task-done'` must return **zero** hits outside the git history. `typecheck` and `lint` will not flag a stale `data-testid` in a feature file, a doc, or a leftover Tailwind class.
4. `bun run test` — unit suites for `@symbiot/editor` (list rendering incl. the decimal regression guard, `removeTaskToggle`), `@symbiot/annotations` (golden `task.md` byte-equality still passes, new unknown-kind decode cases), `@symbiot/ui`, `tailwind-config` (new contrast pair). Use `bun run test` (turbo), not a bare root `bun test` — the latter reports false jsdom failures in this repo.
5. `bun run test:e2e` — BDD suite with the task-checkbox feature removed; no undefined step definitions.
6. `bun run test:e2e:coverage` — BDD branch coverage still ≥ 90% after losing the task scenario (see step 5's coverage note).
7. **Manual check in the running viewer** — open a plan containing both `- [ ]` and `- [x]` items and confirm: bullets aligned with ordinary bullet lists, no checkbox, no decimal numbering, and the done item struck through.

## Post-Implementation

After all implementation steps and verification are complete:

1. **Update documentation (MANDATORY).** In `docs/05-theming.md`, two lines describe `--task-done` in terms of a checkbox that will no longer exist:
   - the token-table row `decorative checkbox accent — not gated` → describe it as the task-annotation accent (still ungated).
   - the sentence "`--task-done` is registered as the `accent-task-done` checkbox accent" → it is consumed as `text-task-done` by the sidebar's task row.

   If step 2 added the `--muted-foreground` / `--background` pair to the contrast test, add its ratios to that same table. No other doc claims the checkbox exists: `docs/03-server-contract.md` and `docs/08-testing.md` describe the feedback format and golden gate, both unchanged, and `docs/06-a11y.md` never listed the checkbox. The repository has no `rfc/` directory, so no RFC version bump applies.

2. Present next actions using AskUserQuestion.

This change is user-facing (the checkbox disappears from the plan surface), so use `--release-notes` in the "Create PR" option.

Tool parameters:
- `question`: "All changes implemented and verified. What's next?"
- `header`: "Next"
- `options`: [
  { label: "Create commit", description: "Run /autopilot:commits-create to commit changes" },
  { label: "Create PR", description: "Run /autopilot:pr-create --release-notes to open a PR with release notes" },
  { label: "Done", description: "No further action needed" }
  ]
- `multiSelect`: false

After the user selects their option:
- "Create commit": invoke `Skill(autopilot:commits-create)`
- "Create PR": invoke `Skill(autopilot:pr-create)` with the flags shown in the option description
- "Done": no further action needed

Base directory for this skill: /Users/tony_vi/.claude/plugins/cache/code-assistants/autopilot/1.10.0/skills/branch:create

# Create Branch

Create a git branch following the repository's naming conventions with GitHub or Linear issue integration. Supports GitHub issue branches (`issue-<number>-<slug>`), Linear ticket branches (`<team>-<number>-<slug>`), and special prefix branches (hotfix, trivial, maintenance, proposal, security).

## When to Use

- When creating a new branch from a GitHub issue
- When creating hotfix, trivial, maintenance, proposal, or security branches
- When invoked from `/autopilot:plan` for automatic branch creation
- When invoked from other skills

## Input

Arguments: `246`

Expected forms:

- `<ISSUE-NUMBER>` — GitHub issue number (e.g., `123` or `#123`). Used to fetch the issue and to build the branch name `issue-<number>-<slug>`.
- `<LINEAR-ID>` — Linear identifier (e.g., `ENG-123`, matching `^[A-Z]+-[0-9]+$`) when the project lists a `linear` tracker in `package.json` `agents.trackers`. Builds `<team>-<number>-<slug>` (the id lowercased).
- `<ISSUE-NUMBER|LINEAR-ID> "<description>"` — issue identifier plus custom branch slug description
- `--start` — Linear only: also move the Linear ticket to "In Progress" after the branch is created (best-effort). Ignored for GitHub and special-prefix branches.
- `--hotfix "<description>"` / `--trivial "<description>"` / `--maintenance "<description>"` / `--proposal "<description>"` / `--security "<description>"` — special prefix branches without a GitHub issue (use `--security` for code-scanning alert fixes → `security-<slug>`)
- `--autopilot` — non-interactive mode used by `/autopilot:run`. Skips the [Phase 5](#phase-5-verify-with-user) confirmation prompt and creates the branch directly with the auto-generated name. Conflict resolution ([Phase 4](#phase-4-check-for-conflicts)) and validation errors still surface.

## Input resolution

Arguments are optional. When `246` is empty OR a field is missing, resolve from context in this order:

- **Issue number** — `246` → parse current branch name for `^issue-([0-9]+)` → prompt user only if none found and no special prefix flag is present.
- **Description** — `246` → generate from GitHub issue title via [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug) rules → no user prompt (auto-generate always succeeds).
- **Special prefix flags** (`--hotfix` / `--trivial` / `--maintenance` / `--proposal` / `--security`) — `246` only. Never inferred. Default: none.
- **`--autopilot`** — `246` only. Never inferred. Default: `false` (interactive mode).
- **Repository conventions** — read `CONTRIBUTING.md` directly from the repository root.

## Phase 0: Preflight Check

Invoke `Skill(autopilot:preflight-check)` with `mode: branch` from this conversation context. The skill validates current branch state, detects stale merged branches, and ensures main is up to date before a new branch is created. If it outputs a "cancelled" message, stop immediately — do not proceed to [Phase 1](#phase-1-input-validation).

## Phase 1: Input Validation

1. **Parse `246`** (shell-quoted positional tokens):
   - Check for `--autopilot`: if present, strip it from the arguments and set `autopilotMode = true`. Otherwise `autopilotMode = false`.
   - Check for `--start`: if present, strip it and set `startIssue = true` (Linear only; see [Phase 6](#phase-6-execute)). Otherwise `startIssue = false`.
   - Check for special prefix flags: `--trivial`, `--hotfix`, `--maintenance`, `--proposal`, `--security`
   - If flag found: extract description from remaining arguments
   - If no flag: extract the first argument as the issue identifier (GitHub number or Linear id), optional description
   - If `246` is empty, fall back to Input resolution (see above).

2. **If special prefix flag detected:**
   - Try to extract description from the conversation history
   - Description is REQUIRED — error if missing: `Description is required for special prefix branches (e.g., /autopilot:branch-create --trivial "fix typo")`
   - Multiple prefix flags not allowed — error: `Only one special prefix flag allowed`
   - Skip [Phase 2](#phase-2-fetch-github-issue) (no GitHub issue to fetch)

3. **If no flag, validate the issue identifier and resolve the provider** (read `package.json` `agents.trackers` with the Read tool):
   - **Linear** — the identifier matches `^[A-Z]+-[0-9]+$` (e.g., `ENG-123`) AND a `linear` tracker is configured: set `provider = linear`.
   - **GitHub** — the identifier matches `^#?[0-9]+$` (strip a leading `#`): set `provider = github`.
   - If invalid: `Invalid issue identifier. Expected a GitHub number (e.g., 123 or #123), a Linear id (e.g., ENG-123) for a linear-tracked project, or a --trivial/--hotfix/--maintenance/--proposal/--security flag`

## Phase 2: Fetch GitHub Issue

**Skip this phase entirely for special prefix flag branches (--hotfix, --trivial, --maintenance, --proposal, --security).**

**If `provider` is `linear`:** fetch the ticket via the Linear MCP `get_issue` tool with `{ "id": "<LINEAR-ID>" }` and read its `title` (for the slug) and `state.name`; if no Linear MCP tool resolves (see the access note below), stop with its `No Linear MCP available …` message instead of continuing without ticket data. Skip the GitHub `gh` steps below and do NOT self-assign — Linear assignment is deferred to a later phase; emit `unassigned — Linear assignment deferred`. Then continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug). The steps below apply to **GitHub** issues only.

<!-- Canonical: [linear:create SKILL.md](../linear:create/SKILL.md#completion-requirement) Linear MCP access note — keep this paragraph in sync with it (only the tool list varies). -->

**Linear MCP access:** Linear operations here use the session's connected Linear MCP server, matching tools by name — the suffix after the final `__` (`get_issue`, `list_issue_statuses`, `save_issue`) — under whatever server prefix the session exposes: the bundled `mcp__plugin_autopilot_linear__*` or a user-configured Linear server such as `mcp__linear-server__*` (Claude Code connects one server per endpoint; a user-scope server shadows the bundled one). The prefix must identify a Linear server (a `linear` server name or the `mcp.linear.app` endpoint) — never bind a generic tool name like `get_issue` to a non-Linear MCP. If a tool is not visible, search for it with ToolSearch by bare tool name before concluding it is absent. Only when no Linear MCP tool resolves under any prefix, stop and tell the user: `No Linear MCP available — check /mcp for a disconnected or unauthenticated Linear server, or connect one: claude mcp add --transport http linear https://mcp.linear.app/mcp`.

1. **Determine the repository** and bind it to `REPO` so every `gh` call in this phase targets the same repo (important in worktrees and multi-remote checkouts):

   ```bash
   REPO=$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner -q .nameWithOwner)
   ```

2. **Fetch the issue** (include `assignees` so the self-assign step needs no extra call):

   ```bash
   gh issue view <ISSUE-NUMBER> -R "$REPO" --json title,body,state,assignees
   ```

3. **Extract:**
   - Issue title (for slug generation)
   - Issue body (for context)
   - Current state (warn if already closed)

4. **If issue not found:**
   - Error: `Issue #<ISSUE-NUMBER> not found in <repo>`

5. **Self-assign the current user** — idempotent and best-effort; it must never block branch creation.

   <!-- Canonical: [resolve-issue-context.md Phase 2](../../agents/resolve-issue-context.md#phase-2-auto-assign-current-user-opt-in) — keep this self-assign algorithm (statuses + steps) in sync with it. -->

   Assigning the issue the moment work starts keeps "who is working on what" accurate. This runs on every issue branch (special-prefix branches skip [Phase 2](#phase-2-fetch-github-issue), so they never assign). On ANY failure, emit the status line and continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug) — the branch is the deliverable; assignment is a side effect.

   Emit exactly one status (same vocabulary as the canonical agent):
   - `@<login> (just assigned)`
   - `@<login> (already assigned)`
   - `unassigned — gh not authenticated`
   - `unassigned — issue closed`
   - `unassigned — permission denied or assignee limit reached`
   - `unassigned — gh edit error: <first line of stderr>`

   Resolve it with these steps:
   1. Resolve the authenticated login (cached 5 minutes):

      ```bash
      LOGIN=$(gh api user --cache 5m --jq .login 2>/dev/null)
      ```

      If `LOGIN` is empty → `unassigned — gh not authenticated`; continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug).

   2. If the issue `state` from step 2 is `CLOSED` → `unassigned — issue closed`; continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug).

   3. Check whether `LOGIN` is already assigned. GitHub logins are `[A-Za-z0-9-]`, so the login is safe to interpolate into a single `gh --jq` expression (gh's `--jq` cannot take `--arg`); `.assignees[]?` tolerates a null or absent array:

      ```bash
      ALREADY=$(gh issue view <ISSUE-NUMBER> -R "$REPO" --json assignees --jq "any(.assignees[]?; .login==\"$LOGIN\")" 2>/dev/null)
      ```

      If `ALREADY == "true"` → `@<LOGIN> (already assigned)`; continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug).

   4. Otherwise attempt the assignment, capturing stderr and exit code (keep this order; read `$?` on the very next line):

      ```bash
      STDERR=$(gh issue edit <ISSUE-NUMBER> -R "$REPO" --add-assignee "$LOGIN" 2>&1 >/dev/null)
      EDIT_EXIT=$?
      ```

   5. **Only when `EDIT_EXIT == 0`**, post-verify with a fresh read, because `gh issue edit --add-assignee` returns exit 0 even when GitHub silently drops the addition (caller lacks `triage`/`write` permission, or the issue is at the 10-assignee limit). When `EDIT_EXIT != 0` the edit never landed, so skip this read and emit `unassigned — gh edit error: <first line of $STDERR>` directly:

      ```bash
      VERIFIED=$(gh issue view <ISSUE-NUMBER> -R "$REPO" --json assignees --jq "any(.assignees[]?; .login==\"$LOGIN\")" 2>/dev/null)
      ```

      - `EDIT_EXIT == 0` AND `VERIFIED == "true"` → `@<LOGIN> (just assigned)`
      - `EDIT_EXIT == 0` AND `VERIFIED != "true"` → `unassigned — permission denied or assignee limit reached`
      - `EDIT_EXIT != 0` → `unassigned — gh edit error: <first line of $STDERR>`

   In all cases, continue to [Phase 3](#phase-3-generate-branch-slug).

## Phase 3: Generate Branch Slug

**If special prefix branch:**

1. Normalize description to lowercase kebab-case
2. Remove special characters (keep only `a-z0-9-`)
3. Construct branch name: `<prefix>-<slug>` (prefix lowercased)
4. Example: `--hotfix` + `"memory leak in editor"` → `hotfix-memory-leak-editor`; `--security` + `"tainted format string"` → `security-tainted-format-string`
5. Validate total length ≤ 100 characters — if over 60, suggest shorter description; if over 100, require it

**If custom description provided:**

1. Normalize to lowercase kebab-case
2. Remove special characters (keep only `a-z0-9-`)
3. Use as the slug

**If no description provided:**

1. Analyze issue title and body
2. Generate a short, meaningful business-focused slug
3. **Rules:**
   - Paraphrased/summarized, NOT mechanical title-to-slug conversion
   - Lowercase with hyphens only
   - 3-5 words maximum
   - Capture the essence of what's being done

**Examples:**

| Issue Title                                                           | Generated Slug       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| "Add JWT token refresh endpoint for authentication service"           | `jwt-refresh`        |
| "Fix race condition in audio streaming when multiple clients connect" | `audio-race-fix`     |
| "Implement user preference settings page with dark mode toggle"       | `user-preferences`   |
| "Refactor database connection pooling for better performance"         | `db-pool-refactor`   |
| "Provide agent prompt to generate branch name"                        | `branch-name-prompt` |

**Construct full branch name:**

- **GitHub:** `issue-<number>-<slug>`
- **Linear:** `<team>-<number>-<slug>` — the Linear id lowercased, then the slug (e.g. `ENG-123` → `eng-123-<slug>`)
- Aim for under 60 characters; reject if over 100
- If too long: regenerate shorter slug

## Phase 4: Check for Conflicts

**Formatting Note:** Do not use markdown formatting (bold, italic, headers) in AskUserQuestion `question` parameter — it renders as raw text. Use plain text with line breaks and simple labels instead.

1. **Check local branches:**

   ```bash
   git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch-name>
   ```

2. **Check remote branches:**

   ```bash
   git ls-remote --heads origin <branch-name>
   ```

3. **Handle conflicts using AskUserQuestion tool:**

   If branch exists locally or remotely, present options:

   Tool parameters:
   - `question`: "Branch <branch-name> already exists. How would you like to proceed?"
   - `header`: "Conflict"
   - `options`: [
     { label: "Checkout existing", description: "Switch to the existing branch" },
     { label: "Create with suffix", description: "Create <branch-name>-2" },
     { label: "Different description", description: "Enter a new description for the slug" }
     ]
   - `multiSelect`: false

## Phase 5: Verify with User

**Autopilot bypass:** If `autopilotMode` is true (from [Phase 1](#phase-1-input-validation)), skip this entire phase and proceed directly to [Phase 6](#phase-6-execute) with the resolved branch name. Do NOT call AskUserQuestion.

Present branch details and confirm using **AskUserQuestion tool**.

**Preview substitution rules (MANDATORY):** The `<number>`, `<slug>`, `<issue title>`, `<prefix>`, and `<PREFIX>` tokens in the templates below are PLACEHOLDERS. Before invoking AskUserQuestion, substitute each placeholder with the concrete value you resolved in earlier phases (e.g., `<number>` → `123`, `<slug>` → `jwt-refresh`, `<issue title>` → `Add JWT token refresh endpoint`). NEVER pass the literal `issue-<number>-<slug>\n\nIssue: <issue title>...` string — every option's `preview` must contain the fully resolved branch preview string. No shorthand (`"..."`, `"<same>"`, empty string) is permitted; always write out the full resolved preview for every option.

**One dialog template for every branch kind.** Tool parameters:

- `question`: "Review the branch name and choose an action."
- `header`: "Create branch"
- `options`: [
  { label: "Create branch", description: "Create and push to origin with tracking", preview: "<preview>" },
  { label: "Edit slug", description: "Modify the branch name slug", preview: "<preview>" }
  ]
- `multiSelect`: false

Both options carry the same `<preview>` content since the user is choosing an action, not content; the shared preview enables a side-by-side layout in the UI. Substitute `<preview>` with the body for the resolved branch kind:

| Branch kind    | `<preview>` body                                                   |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| GitHub issue   | `issue-<number>-<slug>\n\nIssue: <issue title>\nFrom: origin/main` |
| Special prefix | `<prefix>-<slug>\n\nType: <PREFIX>\nFrom: origin/main`             |
| Linear ticket  | `<team>-<number>-<slug>\n\nTicket: <LINEAR-ID>\nFrom: origin/main` |

When a custom description was provided, drop the `Issue:` line (no issue title to show) — e.g. `issue-<number>-<slug>\n\nFrom: origin/main`.

Only proceed to [Phase 6](#phase-6-execute) after user selects "Create branch". If "Edit slug" selected, ask for new slug and regenerate branch name.

## Phase 6: Execute

1. **Fetch latest remote and create branch from origin/main:**

   ```bash
   git fetch origin
   git checkout -b <branch-name> origin/main
   ```

2. **Push with tracking:**

   ```bash
   git push -u origin <branch-name>
   ```

3. **If `provider` is `linear` AND `--start` was passed:** move the ticket to "In Progress" — best-effort, never blocks the branch. Resolve the target state id with the Linear MCP `list_issue_statuses` tool for the ticket's team, then call the Linear MCP `save_issue` tool with `{ "id": "<LINEAR-ID>", "state": "<In Progress state>" }` — tool resolution per the [Phase 2](#phase-2-fetch-github-issue) Linear MCP access note. On success, emit `✓ Ticket <LINEAR-ID> moved to In Progress`; when no Linear MCP tool resolves under any prefix, emit `issue not started — no Linear MCP available (check /mcp or connect one)`; on any other failure, emit `issue not started — <reason>`. Always continue — but the emitted line MUST reach the step 4 output block, never only intermediate text.

4. **Output result:**

   ```
   ✓ Branch created: <branch-name>
   ✓ Pushed to origin with tracking

   Next steps:
   - Make your changes
   - Use /autopilot:commits-create to create commits
   - Use /autopilot:pr-create when ready
   ```

   When `--start` was passed for a Linear ticket, add the step 3 outcome line after the push confirmation — `✓ Ticket <LINEAR-ID> moved to In Progress` on success, or the `issue not started — <reason>` line on failure — so a skipped transition is visible in the final output, not just mid-run.

### Reference formatting & readability

These rules govern references — when you point the reader at a real file, standard, section, commit, or issue. (A token named only as an example, with no real target, is a code specimen in backticks, like any code identifier.) Every reference must resolve: render it as a real link whose target exists, and prefer the most stable link form so it does not rot. Render the same kind of reference the same way everywhere:

- Code specimens — backticks, e.g. `buildReviewComments`, `reviewOutput.ts`. A backticked token names a thing as an example; it is not a reference and carries no link.
- Files, docs, skills, agents, and actions you point the reader at — link them, e.g. `[release field spec](<repo-blob-url>/docs/06-release-field.md)`. Use a repo-relative path in repository files and the absolute `<repo-blob-url>` form in generated output posted outside the repo (PR/issue bodies, review comments, release notes), where relative paths do not resolve. Any prose mention of a file or path that exists in the repo is such a reference — link it so it resolves on the default branch at writing time; a path that does not exist yet (a file the text proposes to create) or one shown inside a command or fenced block is a code specimen, not a reference.
- Standards and conventions — ALWAYS link the versioned RFC by its stable ID, e.g. `[RFC-0001](<repo-blob-url>/rfc/0001-reference-formatting.md)`; an Accepted RFC is immutable except through an explicit version bump, so the link never rots.
- External resources — articles, posts, vendor docs, and web standards or specs you cite — link them inline as `[title](url)` to the canonical source, taking the title from the source (or the site name). Use only a URL present in your input or context — never produce one from memory; a source with no known URL stays plain prose. When several sources back one document, they may be gathered into a short references list.
- Sections — link the heading by its anchor. Same document: a bare `#anchor`, e.g. `[Phase 6](#phase-6-reply-to-review-threads)`. Another document: `path#anchor` — a repo-relative path in repository files, the absolute `<repo-blob-url>/path#anchor` form in generated output. A GitHub anchor is the heading lower-cased, spaces turned to hyphens, punctuation dropped.
- Commit SHAs — ALWAYS a link, e.g. `[0328a61](<repo-commit-url>/0328a61)`; a commit is immutable. If you cannot build the URL, leave the bare SHA un-backticked.
- Issue / PR references — leave the bare number (GitHub auto-links it) or write a full link. A tracker ID GitHub does not auto-link (e.g. Linear `ENG-123`) is dead text when bare: in prose, ALWAYS render it as a markdown link, e.g. `[ENG-123](https://linear.app/<workspace>/issue/ENG-123)` — a slug-less issue URL resolves. /**
 * Decode a list of compact annotation tuples back into AnnotationEntry
 * objects. Ids are synthesized from the tuple position since the wire format
 * doesn't carry them. Callers that need to re-attach anchors should pair
 * this output with `dualAnchor.resolveAnchor` against the current Plate
 * value (Insertion anchors on `contextText`; Replacement on `originalText`).
 *
 * A tuple whose kind this build does not know is skipped rather than thrown on,
 * so a share link written by a newer (or older) encoder still opens with the
 * annotations this build *can* read. Mapping happens before the skip: each
 * decoder derives its entry id from the tuple's position, so dropping tuples
 * first would silently renumber every entry after the gap.
 */
export const decodeAnnotations = (tuples: AnnotationTuple[]): AnnotationEntry[] =>
  tuples
    .map((tuple, i) => {
